headline: Ferrogate's Mass Driver Network Goes Live — 800 Tons an Hour
body:
Ferrogate Transit's long-promised Mass Driver Cargo Network officially entered operation at 06:00 this morning, launching its first commercial payload — 340 tons of Axiom manufacturing components — from the Geartown terminal to a receiving hub in The Spires in under 90 seconds. The electromagnetic launch system, seven years in construction and reportedly costing 14.8 billion quanta, uses a network of accelerator tubes threaded through the Underworld to move sealed cargo pods at speeds exceeding 1,100 kilometers per hour. Ferrogate CEO Nadia Reinholt-Musa called it 'the circulatory system Meridian has been bleeding without for two decades.'

The network's twelve primary nodes connect Geartown, The Circuit, The Spires, and three major transit depots along the outer ring of Meridian 88, with secondary spurs planned through The Narrows by 2148. Ferrogate's launch manifest for the first operational week shows contracts already signed with Axiom, Zheng-Dao, and Palladian — a combined freight volume of 9,400 tons. Competing logistics operators who relied on surface convoy routes expressed alarm, with one anonymous representative telling this station that 'Ferrogate just made half of Meridian's trucking economy obsolete overnight.'

Not everyone is celebrating. Bore Rats, who have operated smuggling networks through the Underworld tunnels for decades, reportedly went dark on all comms as early as last week. Sources in The Underworld suggest the new tube infrastructure cuts directly through three major Bore Rat thoroughfares, and initial construction already collapsed a known safe house near Old Harbor's eastern access points. Ferrogate has deployed Ironclad security contractors to patrol the network corridors, adding another layer of friction to an already volatile underground economy.
aftermath: The Mass Driver Network reduced surface cargo transit times by 74% in its first year, triggering the collapse of seventeen small-to-mid logistics firms and pushing thousands of displaced workers toward The Collective's labor organizing efforts, while Bore Rats spent the following two years rerouting their smuggling corridors around Ferrogate infrastructure.
runner_relevance: The Mass Driver Network's launch created a cascade of runner contracts: Bore Rats immediately began hiring sabotage runners to damage Ferrogate infrastructure nodes and slow encroachment on their corridors, while Ferrogate countered with protection and surveillance runners to guard construction teams. Displaced logistics operators hired intelligence runners to steal Ferrogate's contract manifests. Most lucratively, the new network itself became a premium smuggling vector — runners began taking high-risk courier contracts to slip unregistered cargo pods into the launch queue, bypassing Ironclad inspection checkpoints.
